In tennis, India’s SD Prajwal Dev, partnering France’s Constantin Bittoun Kouzmine, has won his second ATP Challenger doubles title at the Sport Festival Challenger in Phan Thiet, Vietnam.The top-seeded Indo-French duo defeated Japan’s Yamato Sueoka and Naoki Tajima 6-1, 7-6 in the final yesterday. This is Dev’s second ATP Challenger Tour doubles title. His maiden title came in 2023 at the President’s Cup in Kazakhstan, where he partnered fellow Indian Niki Kaliyanda Poonacha.The Challenger 50 event, played on hard courts, began on the 7th of this month and concludes today.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has paid tribute to freedom fighter Jatindranath Das on his death anniversary today.In a social media post, Mr Shah said that even at a young age, Jatindranath Das chose the path of struggle against British rule. The tortures of jail could not shake his resolve.The Minister said that his hunger strike in protest against the inhuman treatment of freedom fighters in jail stands as an example of patriotism and indomitable courage.Mr Shah said Jatindranath Das’s sacrifice and martyrdom will forever inspire the people of the country to serve the nation.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a series of bilateral meetings with his counterparts from Ethiopia, Malaysia and Vietnam as well as the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi. The Prime Minister began his bilateral engagements by holding talks with his Ethiopian counterpart Dr Abiy Ahmed Ali. The Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement that the two leaders held discussions aimed at further strengthening the bilateral Strategic Partnership.Both the leaders reviewed progress across key sectors, including economic cooperation, defence and security partnership, and capacity building. The meeting built on Prime Minister Modi’s historic visit to Addis Ababa in December 2025. The two leaders also exchanged perspectives on regional and international developments of mutual interest and reaffirmed their commitment to close cooperation in multilateral fora. During the meeting, Prime Minister Modi expressed appreciation for Ethiopia’s participation in the 18th BRICS Summit and noted that its presence helped in reinforcing the collective voice of the Global South.The Prime Minister also held bilateral talks with his Malaysian counterpart, Anwar Ibrahim. During the meeting, the two leaders reviewed the progress in bilateral cooperation across a range of areas, including trade and investment, defence and security and people-to-people ties. They also took stock of the outcomes of Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Malaysia in February this year. Mr Modi appreciated Malaysia’s continued support in strengthening ASEAN-India relations. The leaders exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest and expressed their continued commitment to advancing the India-Malaysia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.In the meeting with his Vietnamese counterpart, Le Minh Hung, Prime Minister Modi welcomed Vietnam’s participation in the BRICS Summit as a Partner Country. The Ministry of External Affairs said that the meeting provided an opportunity for both leaders to review the progress made in bilateral ties, which were elevated to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during the State Visit of Vietnamese President To Lam to India in May this year. Both leaders also exchanged views on various regional and global issues of mutual importance and reaffirmed the commitment to further strengthening their partnership. India and Vietnam share a time-tested friendship rooted in shared civilisational heritage, mutual trust and understanding. Vietnam is a key pillar of India’s Act East Policy and an important partner in India’s broader engagement with Southeast Asia.The Prime Minister also held bilateral talks with the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. During the meeting, both sides reiterated the significance of the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which is built on strong political, cultural, commercial, energy, and people-to-people relations. Both sides also agreed that the two countries will continue to work closely to advance shared interests and priorities and further strengthen BRICS cooperation. The two leaders positively noted the announcement by UAE’s International Holding Company to invest in the development of a 11.5 billion US Dollar integrated greenfield aluminium project in Odisha. The project is expected to position Odisha as a global aluminium manufacturing hub.

. Saudi Arabia has temporarily shut down its major East-West oil pipeline, a day after the facility was targeted in a drone attack.  The country’s Ministry of Energy described the shutdown as a precautionary measure.The East-West pipeline has played a key role in Saudi Arabia’s ability to continue exporting oil following the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz during Iran’s war with the US and Israel. The Saudi Foreign Ministry blamed the attack on several drones that came from Iraq. The Iraqi government condemned the assault and ordered an investigation.The shutdown comes as Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen captured port of Mokha and a strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, at the southern entrance to the Red Sea, opening a new front in the ongoing West Asia conflict.The Bab el-Mandeb Strait is one of the world’s key shipping lanes. The advance could boost Iran’s strategy of driving up world oil and gas prices to pressure the United States. Two sources from the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised Yemeni government said its forces had pulled out of Perim and that the Houthis had also taken the ⁠mainland Red Sea coastal town of Dhubab, which faces the island.If the Houthis gain control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz, their backer Iran could gain a critical advantage in its war with the US, reducing supplies through a second major corridor and further raising oil prices.On the other hand, the 1,200-kilometer pipeline shut down by Saudi Arabia is the key alternative route for Kingdom’s oil to reach global markets, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. It has been shipping 4 million to 5 million barrels per day in recent months, amounting to 4  ​to 5 percent of global supply.

. Iraq has dismissed the commander of military operations in Maysan province and reportedly ordered a temporary closure of the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran as a precaution, following an investigation into the drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline.Saudi Arabia had earlier stated that the attacks originated from Iraq but opted not to respond, instead supporting the Iraqi government’s efforts.In Yemen, the Houthis claimed Saudi Arabia carried out more than 100 airstrikes in Yemen over 48 hours, even as Houthis reportedly made major territorial gains along the Red Sea Coast.There were also signs of diplomatic engagement. Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Iranian President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi.It was the highest-level meeting between the two nations since the conflict began. The leaders underscored the importance of supporting efforts to ease tensions, promote de-escalation, and strengthen regional stability.Reports also suggest that Iran and Gulf states are expected to meet in Oman tomorrow to discuss regional issues and the Strait of Hormuz. However, it is uncertain if all countries will participate, and a concrete agreement to reopen the waterway may not be expected immediately.Meanwhile, the Houthi’s advance and the Saudi pipeline attack are adding pressure to an already disrupted regional energy and shipping network, with both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb facing growing security concerns.

The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. The 18th BRICS Summit, under the presidency of India, began in New Delhi. Prime Minister Modi welcomed world leaders at Bharat Mandapam, against the backdrop of the iconic Ramanathaswamy Temple in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu.The two-day grand event brought together eleven Member nations and ten partner countries. During the high-level event, leaders of the BRICS member countries are expected to discuss key issues, including global governance, multilateralism, trade and investment, technology, food and energy security, healthcare, disaster resilience, and critical supply chains. The Summit is being held under India’s 2026 BRICS chairship, with the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”.Several key world leaders are participating in the high-profile summit, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. The BRICS Summit is bringing together 11 major emerging and developing economies, including Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, India, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the UAE. The partner countries are Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam are also participating in the summit.

. The Leaders’ Session of BRICS Business Forum is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.  Heads of State of BRICS Member Countries including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa are attending the session.In his address, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said that during India’s Chairship, BRICS has been driven by a clear purpose, to achieve more balanced trade amongst member nations and to explore expansion of trade in services across the bloc.He said exports from BRICS countries have risen from about USD 900 billion in 2003 to USD 6 trillion in 2024, reflecting the scale of its market and potential.He said, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India remains committed to ensure that this cooperation reaches those who form the backbone of the BRICS economies . Mr Goyal said, it must benefit the farmers, empower women in business and beyond and provide greater opportunities for wealth and prosperity to young entrepreneurs and MSMEs. He said, with the participation over two thousand business leaders and delegates from member countries and partner countries, this is the largest BRICS Business Forum ever held. He mentioned that the Forum has taken up issues such as non-tariff barriers, impacting global value chains, agriculture and agri-technology, services trade, women-led enterprises and the digital economy.

. India’s 2026 BRICS Presidency is broadening historically strong oil-related ties with the Gulf into a wider partnership spanning investment, technology, food security, clean energy and regional stability, a report has said.The report published in a daily published from UAE said energy ties remain the foundation of the relationship at the 18th BRICS Summit, but cooperation is expanding into new strategic areas. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the UAE this year, both the countries deepened collaboration on crude oil, LNG and LPG, and agreed to increase UAE participation in India’s strategic petroleum reserves and explored strategic gas reserves.Another area of co-operation is food-security which can link Gulf demand with India’s agricultural and food-processing capabilities. Investment in storage, logistics and reliable supply chains can be explored, the report noted. Highlighting the timing of the event, the report said that regional tensions have renewed attention on energy security, maritime trade and safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while Gulf states diversify their economies, invest in advanced technology and strengthen commercial links with Asia.The Gulf is represented in the expanded BRICS through Saudi Arabia and the UAE, providing the bloc greater weight in the global energy and finance landscape. India-Gulf ties grew stronger in February this year, when the country signed terms of reference with GCC and formally launched negotiations for a comprehensive free trade agreement, covering Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

. Today is the second and final day of the BRICS summit. Today BRICS Member and Partner Countries will participate in the session based on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.The ten partner countries are  Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.After the conclusion of the session, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold bilateral meetings with Presidents of Kazakhstan, Philippines, Egypt, South Africa and Burundi. He will also hold meetings with Vice Presidents of Nigeria and Uganda.The Summit is being held under India’s BRICS chairship, with the theme, Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. With BRICS team, Anand Kumar, Akashvani News Delhi.The two-day summit began yesterday at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The BRICS nations adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026 on the first day of the Summit itself. The BRICS nations reiterated their commitment to the peaceful resolution of international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy.The leaders also expressed their concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation.They also strongly condemned the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April last year in the strongest terms and reaffirmed their commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. India is organising the Summit for the fourth time.

. Iran and Oman have agreed on new entry and exit shipping routes for the Strait of Hormuz, which they plan to present to other Gulf nations at an upcoming regional meeting.Under this new plan, the entry route into the Gulf will sit entirely within Iranian territorial waters, and a section of the exit route will also fall under Iranian control. Once this new system starts operating, the waterway’s southern route will be closed, directly opposing the United States’ demands to keep it open.Furthermore, Iranian officials emphasised that this agreement does not mean the Strait of Hormuz is being reopened. Iran has set seven conditions for the U.S. before the waterway can open, and it will remain closed until those demands are met.Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei announced on Friday that Gulf littoral states’ foreign ministers are scheduled to meet in Oman tomorrow to exchange views on regional issues, including the Iran-Oman talks on designating safe routes in the Strait of Hormuz.

. India has set the Guinness World Record with World’s Longest Steel Slag Road at Raigarh in Chhattisgarh. The 1.85-kilometre road marks a major scale-up of an indigenous technology that converts processed steel slag, a by-product of steel production, into aggregates for road construction.Speaking at the conferment ceremony of the Guinness World Record in New Delhi today, Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh said that Steel Slag Road Technology can reduce road construction costs by around 40 per cent while delivering four times the strength of conventional roads. He said that this technology is being pursued by CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI) New Delhi with private sector participation.Dr Singh said that this initiative simultaneously lives up to more than one flagship priorities of this government emphasising on Waste to Wealth recycling options. He said that the technology can also substantially extend the maintenance cycle, with a re-look required only after about 15 years in suitable applications, making it a breakthrough with implications not only for road engineering but also for the overall infrastructure economy.The Minister called for the indigenous technology to move from one project to many projects and from one State to many States, with its adoption extending beyond the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to Railways, other Government departments, State Governments and private builders.

. Describing sport as a vehicle for social development, the BRICS New Delhi Declaration today backed India’s twin proposals of forming a Working Group on Sports Technology and the organisation of a Sports Goods Manufacturing Conclave for enhanced cooperation among member nations. The Declaration recognised the increasing role of technology in enhancing quality of performance, welfare, governance and inclusion in sports and encouraged discussions on the formation of the Working Group on Sports Technology.Emphasising the importance of sport as a vehicle for social development, the Declaration called for people-to-people exchanges and promotion of healthy and active societies. The working group on Sports Technology and the conclave for sports goods manufacturers were among the three key initiatives that Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya listed during the BRICS Sports Ministers’ meet in Visakhapatnam last month under India’s Chairship.

. In cricket, India will begin their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan at Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi tomorrow. All three matches are scheduled at the same venue. India have won eight of their nine T20Is against Afghanistan, with one match ending without a result. The Indian team will look to build momentum after defeats against Ireland and England in the new T20 cycle.

. In tennis, Kazakhstan’s Elena Rybakina defeated Belarusian Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to win the US Open women’s singles final at Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York last night.This is Rybakina’s first US Open title and her third career Grand Slam championship, following her Australian Open victory earlier in the year. With the win, Rybakina officially takes over the WTA world No. 1 ranking from Sabalenka.Earlier, American Christian Harrison and Britain’s Neal Skupski clinched the men’s doubles title, defeating Germany’s Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz.The American-British pair won the final 6-4, 7-6 to claim their second Grand Slam title of the year, after their Australian Open victory in January.The men’s singles final will be played between Germany’s World No. 2 Alexander Zverev and local favourite Ben Shelton in New York tonight. The match is scheduled to begin at 11:30 PM Indian time.

Markets regulator SEBI on Saturday proposed changes to the methodology for calculating expiry-day settlement prices of index and stock derivatives, following a review of the newly introduced closing auction session (CAS) framework.In a consultation paper, SEBI proposed two options for determining the settlement prices, a blended Volume Weighted Average Price – VWAP based on trades executed during the last 30 minutes of the continuous trading session – CTS, and the 10-minute CAS, or continuation of the existing CTS VWAP methodology. The proposals follow feedback received from market participants on the use of the CAS-determined closing price for settling derivative contracts on expiry. Determination of derivative settlement prices based on the closing price arrived at through CAS was among the significant areas of feedback received by SEBI.SEBI introduced the CAS framework in the equity cash segment from August 3 to determine the closing price of securities. Under the current framework, the closing price determined through CAS also serves as the basis for determining settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry. The use of the CAS-determined closing price for expiry-day settlement of derivatives has been one of the key concerns raised by market participants, prompting Sebi to review the existing methodology.On 3rd September, SEBI had said it may propose changes to the methodology following the feedback and indicated that a consultation paper on the proposed framework was likely to be released in about a week. The proposed changes are aimed at addressing concerns around the use of the CAS-determined closing price as the basis for settling derivative contracts on expiry. The Securities and Exchange Board of India – SEBI has sought comments from stakeholders on the proposals till 3rd October.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President of China, Xi Jinping today reaffirmed that India and China should take a strategic and long term perspective of their ties and that differences should not become disputes. During their bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit, the two leaders welcomed the steady progress in India-China bilateral relations since their last meeting in Tianjin in August last year.Prime Minister Modi highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals – mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest. He emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remain an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.The two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples. External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that the two leaders took note of the progress in people-to-people ties and underscored the need to further promote cultural exchanges, business linkages and greater mobility between the two countries.On economic and trade relations, they underlined the need to address each other’s concerns, including structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues, and facilitation of meaningful and predictable market access. The two leaders agreed that both sides must continue to expand common ground on regional and global issues and in addressing challenges. Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Modi held a series of bilateral meetings with leaders of BRICS countries.

The Archery Premier League (APL) is set for a bigger second season, with 36 of India’s leading archers set to compete alongside 12 international stars from 10 countries in Hyderabad from October 8 to 18. The expanded field brings together Olympic medallists, world champions, World Cup winners and some of the biggest names in the sport, adding further international flavour to the six-franchise competition.Four-time Olympian Deepika Kumari and World Championship silver medallist Atanu Das headline India’s recurve contingent, with reigning Asian champion Dhiraj Bommadevara also part of the field. The compound section features multi-time World Cup and Asian Games champion Jyothi Surekha Vennam, former World No. 1 Abhishek Verma and former World Champion Ojas Pravin Deotale.The international contingent is led by Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion Mete Gazoz of Türkiye, Paris 2024 bronze medallist Casey Kaufhold of the United States, Brazil’s World No. 1 Marcus D’Almeida and Great Britain’s World No. 2 Ella Gibson. Dutch compound star Mike Schloesser, a former World Champion and four-time World Cup Final winner, will also compete.The league will also feature all 12 members of India’s Asian Games-bound archery squad, giving the APL added relevance ahead of the country’s campaign in Aichi-Nagoya later this month. Among those entering the league for the first time are World Championships silver medallist Rajat Chauhan, World Cup stage gold medallist Ridhi, World University Games gold medallist Kushal Dalal and junior national champion Kirti Sharma.The second season will retain one of the league’s most distinctive features – its 15-second shot clock. Five seconds quicker than the standard Olympic timing, the format is designed to place greater emphasis on speed, decision-making and composure under pressure. Initiated by the Archery Association of India with the support of the Government of Telangana, the league will feature six mixed-gender franchise teams competing across the Recurve and Compound categories. The 11-day tournament will be held at People’s Plaza on Hyderabad’s Necklace Road. Rajputana Royals won the inaugural edition, which also generated significant digital engagement among younger audiences.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today discussed opportunities to further deepen the India – Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) partnership. The Finance Minister met the President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Zou Jiayi, in New Delhi. In a social media post, the Finance Ministry said discussions were held on supporting India’s infrastructure and transport connectivity priorities, enhancing local-currency financing, increasing private-sector participation and the global presence of AIIB.

. The three-day Dryland Congress 2026 concluded in New Delhi with a call for greater South-South and triangular cooperation to accelerate solutions for dryland agriculture.The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare said that the event culminated with the adoption of the Delhi Declaration on Drylands (3D).The declaration set out a shared agenda for transforming dryland agriculture through collaboration, knowledge exchange, innovation and collective action across the Global South.The Ministry added that the meeting affirmed a renewed commitment to translate scientific knowledge into action, scale proven innovations and strengthen partnerships for resilient and sustainable dryland agriculture across the Global South.On the occasion, the Secretary in the Department of Agricultural Research and Education and Director General of ICAR, Dr M. L. Jat stressed the need for robust data and information systems for dryland agri-food systems, as well as common innovation grounds or living laboratories that connect research with practice and policy.

. China Southern Airlines said today it will resume regular passenger flights between Guangzhou and New Delhi from 21st of this month, ending a six-year suspension. Air services between India and China were suspended after the COVID-19 pandemic began in 2020.The resumption comes as Chinese President Xi Jinping visits India for the BRICS summit and holds talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.In March this year, Indian carrier IndiGo also began daily flights between Shanghai and Kolkata, further expanding air links between India and China.

. In Nepal, the death toll from flash floods has risen to 1,386, with more bodies recovered from eight affected districts.The floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on 26th of last month, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 104 of the recovered bodies have so far been identified and handed over to families. Around 5,130 people are still reported missing.Security forces continue search and rescue operations. More than 13,700 people have been rescued so far, while 339 people are undergoing treatment in hospitals.Meanwhile, over 3,700 people are staying in temporary shelters across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts.

. England moved a little closer to India in the World Test Championship (WTC) points table after beating Pakistan in the third Test at Edgbaston, Birmingham. Pakistan have lost further ground in the WTC standings, being already at the dead bottom ahead of the Birmingham loss. England have consolidated their sixth spot in the nine-team standings.Australia continue to hold the top spot in the WTC standings. South Africa occupy the second spot, followed by New Zealand. Bangladesh are ahead of India and occupy the fourth spot. Sri Lanka and West Indies are seventh and eighth, respectively, in the points table. The top two will secure the places for the WTC final from June 9 to 13.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that inflows through the Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] and the other schemes have been ‘very robust’. In an interview with a private television channel, the RBI Governor said the strong inflows reflect confidence in India’s macroeconomic fundamentals and demonstrate the ability to attract foreign capital within a short period.On the surplus liquidity in the banking system, Malhotra said the Reserve Bank has enough tools at its disposal to manage liquidity and is prepared to use them as needed. He added that some of the surplus liquidity would be withdrawn over time through currency circulation, forex intervention and banks’ reserve requirements amid rising credit growth. Malhotra added that the central ​bank’s objective was to maintain appropriate liquidity conditions and keep the weighted average call rate aligned with the repo rate.The RBI Governor said the Monetary Policy Committee would reassess growth and inflation dynamics at its meeting next month amid rising prices of crude oil owing to the ongoing West Asia crisis. Sanjay Malhotra noted that the impact of higher crude prices on inflation would depend on the extent to which the increase is passed through to consumers.He said the government has to a great degree, absorbed and cushioned the shock; as a result, the Indian economy has weathered it well. On stronger-than-expected growth in the April to June quarter, the RBI Governor said it was not entirely surprising. He added that incoming corporate data was also pointing to firmer growth. The central bank saw no signs of overheating, including in consumption loans.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. In the T20 Women’s Asia Cup final, India will face defending champions Sri Lanka in Dubai today. The summit clash will begin at 8 PM Indian time.Seven-time champions India reached the final unbeaten, topping Group A with three wins before defeating Bangladesh by 40 runs in the semi-final.Sri Lanka also secured their spot in the final, winning all three of their group matches before defeating Pakistan by four wickets in the semi-final.Although India remains the most successful team in Women’s Asia Cup history with seven titles, Sri Lanka had previously defeated them in a 2024 title clash, securing their maiden Asia Cup crown.

. A human rights body in Pakistan has accused authorities of pursuing a systematic campaign of militarisation and repression in Balochistan, where violence and displacement have become part of civilians’ everyday lives. The rights body said that the discovery of mutilated bodies of Baloch civilians abandoned along roadsides reflects the brutality and inhumanity of the violence.Expressing grave concern over the deteriorating situation in Balochistan’s Mastung district, the rights body said that orchards which provide livelihoods to thousands of people in the region now face destruction under what it described as a state policy, threatening both land and livelihoods. It said such incidents cannot be brushed aside as collateral damage but must be seen as the human cost of a policy imposed on the people of Balochistan by Pakistani authorities.

. President Droupadi Murmu today conveyed greetings to her Israeli counterpart, Isaac Herzog and the Jewish community across Israel and the world on the Jewish New Year, Rosh Hashanah. In a social media post, the President wished that the new year usher in peace, prosperity, good health and renewed hope for all.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. BRICS leaders have condemned the April 2025 Pahalgam terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir. In a joint statement, BRICS leaders have called for zero tolerance towards terrorism, reaffirming the regional bloc’s commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms.The New Delhi Declaration, adopted unanimously on the opening day of the summit, said that all acts of terrorism are criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation and who committed such an act.Akashvani correspondent reports that the New Delhi declaration condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April 2025, during which 26 people were killed and many more injured. The attack was later traced to terrorists backed and trained in Pakistan.The declaration also called for action against the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing, and safe havens.BRICS leaders also urged the member nations to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards in countering terrorism. They further called for concerted actions against all UN-designated terrorists and terrorist entities.The joint declaration also expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint and for avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation.It said the BRICS countries will increase efforts, through dialogue and diplomacy, towards a long-term understanding that will contribute to lasting peace, security and stability in the region.BRICS leaders also stressed the need to work together to maintain a smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law.The BRICS bloc expressed concern about the ongoing conflicts in many parts of the world and the current state of polarisation and fragmentation in the international order.

. In Hockey, India stormed into the final of the Women Junior Asia Cup 2026 defeating South Korea 5-1 in Moqi, China today.India will face host China in the final clash of the tournament. For India Supriya scored a hat trick, while Madhu Sidar and Sukhveer Kaur also found the net for India. While Yuri Jeong scored South Korea’s only goal of the match.The victory follows India’s 19-0 quarterfinal win over Pakistan. India topped its group, which also included Japan, Malaysia and South Korea. India is seeking a third consecutive Women’s Junior Asia Cup title after winning the tournament in 2023 and 2024.

. BRICS nations have unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration on the First day of the BRICS Summit 2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed to adopt the declaration at the end of the session on the first day of the summit.In his closing remarks, the Prime Minister noted that the New Delhi Declaration adopted today provides a clear direction for the shared resolve of the member countries. He added that it is now their shared responsibility to translate these resolutions into tangible results.The Prime Minister said that today’s discussion makes it evident that the changing world cannot be steered by outdated institutions and underlined that reforms are essential in representation, responsiveness, and rule-making. Mr Modi said that the leaders also emphasised that the Global South must have equal participation in the development of future technologies and the rules governing them.He emphasised that the gap between decisions and their outcomes must be bridged through partnership and collective action. The Prime Minister also expressed his gratitude to the leaders for their valuable contributions, constructive spirit and commitment as the BRICS Chair. To mark the 20 years of BRICS, two commemorative postage stamps were also released by the leaders of the member countries on this occasion.Earlier in his opening remarks on the first day of the session, which was based on inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism, Mr Modi proposed a BRICS Continuity and Implementation Mechanism to ensure that the grouping’s institutional momentum is maintained despite the Chairship changing every year.In his opening remarks at today’s session of the BRICS Summit 2026, which is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Mr Modi said the mechanism would enable follow-up of all initiatives and outcomes through the Troika. The Prime Minister said BRICS countries will have to work on a new and ambitious agenda for the next 20 years. He said the process must begin with the grouping’s own working system.The Prime Minister also proposed to establish a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect the maritime authorities and diplomatic missions of relevant countries to facilitate assistance during difficult times. Mr Modi observed that seafarers make a massive contribution to global trade, yet they often find themselves lacking support during difficult times.Mr Modi said the time has come to translate the unity and consensus among BRICS countries into concrete outcomes on the global stage. He stressed that BRICS members respect one another and move forward through consensus. He said the grouping is not working against anyone, but is moving forward with the approach of taking everyone along.The Prime Minister described this year’s BRICS Summit as a historic milestone, noting that the grouping is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. He said BRICS is at its coming-of-age moment and has established its distinct identity on the global stage over the past two decades.Mr Modi said India’s Chairship of BRICS is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. He said Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability have been India’s foremost priorities as Chair. Guided by these priorities, India has laid special emphasis on connecting BRICS cooperation directly with the common people.The Prime Minister noted that with this vision, more than 350 meetings were organised, and India had the privilege of welcoming delegations across nearly 30 cities in the country.In his address, the Prime Minister noted that the Global South stands in the front row of global crises but in the back row of decision-making. He emphasised transforming this ‘pyramid of privilege’ into a ‘platform of partnership’. In this context, the Prime Minister proposed to jointly formulate 10 proposals for global governance reform, aiming to shape them into a BRICS reform roadmap by the time of the next Summit.On the issue of reform in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), the Prime Minister emphasised that reform of the UNSC can no longer be postponed and negotiations on this matter must be linked to a definite time frame and clear outcomes. He said, similarly, voting power, leadership positions, and policy priorities within financial institutions must align with today’s economic realities.He mentioned that countries that drive global economic growth should also play an appropriate role in shaping global economic governance. Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the leaders of BRICS Member countries during their arrivals at the Bharat Mandapam for the Summit.

. Union Health Minister JP Nadda has stated that safeguarding public health is essential for national security. He was speaking after inaugurating 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories in Andhra Pradesh today, in the presence of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and State Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav.Mr Nadda said the new facilities will strengthen the State’s ability to provide critical care and detect disease threats early. He said the COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the need for health infrastructure that can respond to emergencies without affecting routine healthcare services. The Minister said the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission was launched with this objective.Under the scheme, 631 Critical Care Blocks have been sanctioned across the country. In Andhra Pradesh, one thousand 271 crore 80 lakh rupees has been allocated for the five-year scheme period under four key components of Critical Care Blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories, Urban Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and Rural Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.Mr. Nadda said 24 Critical Care Blocks have been sanctioned in Andhra Pradesh at an estimated cost of about 606 crore rupees. He said more than one lakh 75 thousand Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have been established across the country to provide comprehensive primary healthcare closer to people’s homes. He highlighted the progress in screening for diabetes, hypertension and various cancers, along with the introduction of HPV vaccination.He also noted improvements in maternal and child health indicators, TB control and reduction in out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure. The Minister praised Andhra Pradesh’s Sanjeevani programme for providing testing for 41 health parameters closer to communities and expressed interest in exploring its replication at the national level.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that India should pursue technological innovation at scale, but without compromising human responsibility, safety and public trust.Addressing the Global Fintech Festival 2026, the Finance Minister said India’s young generation was not waiting for opportunities but was creating platforms, enterprises and new solutions. She said India’s demographic dividend was visible in the country’s rapidly growing technology and fintech ecosystem.Smt. Sitharaman also questioned those who view India’s demographic dividend through a lens of perpetual pessimism. Referring to sceptics in a lighter vein, she said “naraz fufa jis” are never short of reasons to doubt India’s moment and capabilities.Highlighting the challenges posed by emerging technologies, the Finance Minister described Artificial Intelligence as a double-edged sword. She said AI can help detect fraud faster, but can also enable perpetrators to automate larger and more sophisticated frauds.Finance Minister stressed the need for greater institutional accountability in the development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence. She said speed and efficiency should not come at the cost of safety, transparency and human oversight. Regulators, boards and senior management, she said, must understand how AI is used, the decisions it influences and the risks involved.She also called for stronger cybersecurity, data protection, consumer protection and cooperation between regulators and innovators. The Finance Minister said the success of India’s fintech sector should be measured not only by transactions and valuations, but also by the trust it earns and the problems it solves.Smt. Sitharaman also urged the Reserve Bank of India to further advance its wholesale and retail Central Bank Digital Currency pilots, citing the growing momentum in tokenisation and digital finance.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today met the Iranian Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance, Seyed Ali Madanizadeh, in New Delhi. Ms Sitharaman thanked Iran for its participation in the BRICS Summit and its productive engagement in the deliberations in the Finance Track.The Ministry of Finance informed that during the meeting, both sides exchanged views on issues related to economic growth and the potential for cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

. In Men’s cricket, India will begin their three-match Twenty20 International series against Afghanistan today at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi. The first match will start at 7 PM Indian time.The second T20I will be played on Tuesday, followed by the third and final match on Thursday. All three games will be held at the same venue and begin at the same time.T20 captain Shreyas Iyer will lead the Indian side, with Tilak Varma as his deputy. The pace attack includes Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh and Yash Thakur.Wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson returns to the squad, while spinner Varun Chakaravarthy is also back after recovering from injury. Teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has also been named in the team.India have dominated their head-to-head record against Ibrahim Zadran-led Afghanistan, winning eight of their nine T20Is. One match ended without a result.

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. . The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

The Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India (ASSOCHAM) has hailed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision for strengthening BRICS as a powerful platform for global cooperation and a stronger voice for the Global South. President of ASSOCHAM Nirmal K Minda said that the Prime Minister’s vision of transforming BRICS cooperation into concrete business outcomes is highly significant. He added that deepening trade, investment, technology, start-up and business partnerships among BRICS economies can unlock enormous opportunities and create new avenues for inclusive and sustainable growth.Mr Minda said that the emphasis on innovation, digital solutions, infrastructure, strategic technologies and initiatives such as the BRICS Startup Innovation Fund can further strengthen collaboration and enable Indian enterprises to scale globally.

A special cultural performance, Navarasa – The Universe of Shared Emotions, was presented during the BRICS Leaders’ Summit Gala Dinner hosted by the Prime Minister at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi yesterday evening.The cultural event featured the BRICS Symphony – One Rhythm, Many Cultures, bringing together musicians from BRICS Members and Partner countries in a unique collaborative musical performance.Drawing on diverse musical traditions, the Symphony created a shared artistic expression that reflected the diversity, cultural richness and spirit of togetherness of the BRICS family.The Symphony showcased different instruments from BRICS countries and found synergy of music and India’s classical dance traditions with BRICS bridging musical cultures across nations. The musical event embodied the spirit of Building a Better World Together through cultural exchanges.It celebrated the diversity of artistic expressions, human experiences and human bonding. The BRICS Symphony showcased the rich cultures and diverse civilisations of BRICS, anchored in India’s unique quality of being the land of cultural diversity.

. The death toll from a passenger ferry fire in the Philippines rose to 76 today after rescuers recovered more remains. Forty-three of the 132 people aboard survived the Wednesday night fire, while 13 remain missing. The ferry was sailing from Manila to Coron in southwestern Palawan province when the fire broke out about 39 kilometres from its destination. The cause remains under investigation.

. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) today successfully secured the extradition of Red Notice subject Amritpal Singh alias Gurpal Singh from Moldova to India. The wanted fugitive was extradited by the CBI in coordination with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and Punjab Police.A team of four members of Punjab Police was sent to Moldova to bring back the fugitive. The investigation agency said that he was wanted in multiple serious criminal cases registered in Punjab. The criminal offences include double murder with the use of firearms, offences under the Arms Act and NDPS Act. The fugitive is also charged with using forged documents and violations of the Passport Act.The CBI also underlined that in the last few years 175 wanted criminals have been brought back to India. To make such extraditions possible, CBI works as the National Central Bureau for INTERPOL in India. The agency coordinates with all Law Enforcement Agencies in India through BHARATPOL for assistance via INTERPOL channels.
